newsitem.title: UK: UK's Rifkind fears war over Cyprus.
newsitem.headline: UK's Rifkind fears war over Cyprus.

text.p: British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said on Tuesday there was a serious possibility of Greece and Turkey going to war over Cyprus.
Rifkind, speaking on BBC Radio, also accused Athens and Ankara of lacking the political will to find a solution.
"When relations are already bad and tense and difficult and both sides appear to be looking for an excuse to make them worse, that is pretty grim," he said.
Asked whether there might be conflict between Greece and Turkey in the Aegean, Rifkind said: "It has to be a serious possibility."
"I am not as confident as logic would imply because there has been a real lack of political will on both sides," he said.

Britain expressed alarm last month over a Greek Cypriot decision to buy Russian surface-to-air missiles, saying it could destabilise what is already one of the most heavily militarised areas of the world.
On a visit to the divided island in December, Rifkind told Greek Cypriot leaders the planned purchase would be a "big step in the wrong direction."

The planned acquisition of the S-300 system would neutralise the air superiority Turkey has had since 1974 when its troops invaded the northern third of Cyprus in response to a short-lived coup engineered by the military then ruling Greece.
Tension has increased perceptibly on the island in the past six months after the deaths of four people in ceasefire line incidents and both sides continue to build up their defences.
